ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the experiment studying the self-induction phenomenon, two completely identical bulbs A and B, a coil L with a very large self-inductance coefficient, and a fixed resistor R are used to form the circuit shown in Figure 5 (the DC resistance of the coil can be neglected, and the internal resistance of the power supply cannot be neglected). Regarding this experiment, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: At the instant the switch is closed, B lights up before A, and then B gradually becomes dimmer

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the self-induction phenomenon experiment shown in Figure 5, at the instant the switch is closed, which of bulbs A and B lights up first?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the circuit in the figure, the left and right sides are common nodes, forming parallel branches; in the upper branch, bulb B is on the left, fixed resistor R is on the right, and the two are connected in series; in the middle branch, coil L is on the left, bulb A is on the right, and the two are connected in series; below there is a power supply and switch S, and after S is closed, power is supplied to these two branches. Then reason: the problem stem states that the self-inductance coefficient of coil L is very large. At the instant the switch is closed, the current through the branch where coil L is located must start increasing from zero, and the coil will generate a self-induced electromotive force to hinder the increase of the current, so the current in the L-A branch where A is located cannot immediately reach a value that makes the bulb glow obviously. In the upper branch B-R, there is no inductive element hindering a sudden change in current, and after the switch is closed, current can immediately pass through bulb B. Therefore, at the instant the switch is closed, bulb B lights first.
